sections.executive_summary:
OzMart’s warehouse combines 137,901 order items in a star schema for customer, product, supplier, calendar and regional analysis. Delivered orders provide a completed-sales measure. Profit cannot be estimated without product costs and freight.

The leading age group by revenue varies across states, from age 19 in ACT to age 85 in Tasmania. Toys & Games leads delivered unit sales in all eight states, including 24,667 units in NSW. The supplier query returns five NSW-based suppliers for each year. Erin Marquez leads 2022 and 2023 with 833 and 598 units. These findings can inform regional stock and supplier reviews, although they describe the supplied period rather than future demand.

The loan analysis compares logistic regression and a decision tree using 9,998 labelled records, an 80/20 stratified split and five-fold cross-validation within training data. Logistic regression has test AUC 0.625, compared with 0.500 for the tree. Both miss every held-out default. Accuracy around 89% therefore provides little assurance about credit risk. Neither model should determine lending eligibility. Further analysis requires predictors recorded before default, training-based threshold selection and independent validation, supported by privacy safeguards and human review.
sections.query_4_1: Revenue is SUM(LineAmount) for delivered items, grouped by customer destination state and exact source age. DENSE_RANK retains all age groups sharing the highest revenue (Microsoft, 2026). The result contains one winner per state: ACT 19, NSW 57, NT 71, QLD 40, SA 81, TAS 85, VIC 35 and WA 31. NSW age 57 contributes 44,167.3311 in the source currency. These are aggregate revenue profiles, not per-customer spending estimates; cohort size and purchase frequency may explain differences. No currency conversion or causal targeting effect is assumed.
sections.query_4_2: Product type means the product category, and best-selling means delivered units rather than revenue or distinct order lines. Ranking is partitioned by customer destination state; DENSE_RANK retains tied category positions. The actual output has five categories in each of eight states, with no included ties. Toys & Games ranks first everywhere: NSW contributes 24,667 units, VIC 17,914 and QLD 17,836. Revenue is shown as supporting context. The result supports category-level stock review, but does not reveal margins, inventory availability or future demand.
sections.query_4_3: The query defines NSW suppliers by their own location and sums delivered quantities by purchase year. ROW_NUMBER orders units descending, then SellerID ascending to resolve ties consistently. It returns exactly five suppliers in each of 2021, 2022 and 2023: 15 rows overall. Michelle Wells leads 2021 with 23 units; Erin Marquez leads 2022 and 2023 with 833 and 598. The conflicting location recorded as UNK is excluded because its state cannot be established. Supplier location answers the question about NSW-based providers; customer destination would describe a different market. Annual differences may partly reflect unequal observation periods.
